english.title: Withholding information about commission of act prejudicial to State
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having been required in pursuance of an authorisation under section 6(1) of the Official Secrets Act 1920 to

(A)_[give information, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..),]_
(B)_[attend **(..SPECIFY PLACE..) at **(..SPECIFY TIME AND DATE..),]_

(C)_[failed to comply with that requirement]_
(D)_[knowingly gave false information, namely **(..SPECIFY FALSE INFORMATION..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(1) and 8(2) of the Official Secrets Act 1920.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Whilst this offence is triable either way, it should usually be dealt with on indictment. The offence may only be dealt with summarily with the consent of the Attorney General (section 8(2) Official Secrets Act 1920).

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
